title: After a confirmed resubmit refusal, re-read the task and its evidence and hand the new check evidence to the evaluator
outcome: When Engram refuses an evaluator's submission with acceptance_evaluation_resubmit and the refusal is confirmed, the host reads the task and its evidence again and gives the evaluator the new cut and the new check evidence, said openly; it never re-injects the old cut and never advances the cut silently.
acceptance: An uncertain earlier submission is settled first by reading its exact record or resending the stored key and payload unchanged, before refreshing the task target or minting a new key. A later refusal alone does not settle an earlier unknown send. Tests preserve the original arguments and refuse target replacement while uncertainty remains.

After a confirmed typed acceptance_evaluation_resubmit refusal, the host rereads the task, canonical identity, cut, check evidence, policy, pin, source, carried failure and open obligations; persists and acknowledges the new target; and presents the old and new cuts and newly recorded check evidence in a host-authored brief under a fresh ordinal-bearing key. Changes are presentation only: the evaluator freshly judges every criterion against all evidence through the new cut, and the host supplies no verdict. Tests show the fresh brief and no old-cut reinjection.
TermAl's specification of the host's acceptance-evaluation procedure describes this path and links Engram's section 'Evaluation unit and re-evaluation'.
The full five-stage gate passes on the exact reviewed tree, its run directory and fingerprint cited in a note.

The host never submits verdicts with a cut the evaluator was not shown, and never resubmits the earlier verdicts without a fresh judgment by the evaluator; a test shows that the old cut is not re-injected and the cut is not advanced silently.

Only a confirmed typed acceptance_evaluation_resubmit refusal starts this refresh path. Unknown outcomes, other refusals, and source/root changes preserve their existing distinct dispositions. Engram's already-passed-check exception for the declared source revision remains effective; a late append alone does not force resubmission. Tests discriminate these cases.
